function.name: concert_finder
function.description: Locate upcoming concerts based on music genre in specified city and state. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

location.description: The city and state to find concerts.

time_period.description: Number of days to search upcoming concerts.

message.reasoning:
The user wants to find upcoming concerts in the next month in California San Francisco and New York for rock and jazz genres. We need to call the function concert_finder twice: once for San Francisco with music_genre "rock" and "jazz"? Actually we might need separate calls for each genre? The function signature expects one music_genre string. So we can call it twice per location: one for rock, one for jazz. Or we could combine them into a single string like "rock,jazz". But likely we should do separate calls.

We need to provide location: "San Francisco, CA" or "San Francisco, California" and "New York, NY" or "New York, New York".

Time period default is 30 days. So we don't need to specify time_period.

Thus we will call concert_finder twice for San Francisco: first with music_genre "rock", second with "jazz". Then same for New York.

But maybe we can combine all four queries into two calls: one for San Francisco with music_genre "rock" and "jazz" combined? But the function expects a string; we could pass "rock, jazz" but not sure if accepted. Safer to do separate calls.

So we will call the function twice for each location. That means total 4 calls. But we can also call it once for each location with music_genre "rock" and then again with "jazz". We'll do that.

We'll produce calls accordingly.
